# Accessibility Audit

Use this skill when reviewing or improving interface accessibility.

## Checklist
- Ensure sufficient color contrast for text and UI controls.
- Keep focus indicators visible and strong.
- Use semantic headings, lists, buttons, and landmarks correctly.
- Make all major interactions keyboard accessible.
- Keep content readable, structured, and resilient to zoom.

## Quality bar
- Users should be able to navigate the interface without a mouse.
- Contrast and typography must remain legible across the design.
- Motion and state changes should not reduce clarity or usability.

## Example
- Strong: visible focus ring, accessible link labels, clear buttons, and readable contrast.
- Weak: white text on a light background or a button that is visually styled but not keyboard focusable.
